summary: 115 Vicarage Road is a detached, two-storey, white-rendered inter-war house with a hipped plain-tile main roof and a mock-Tudor gabled two-storey bay to the front left. It has an integral front garage (street-right) with a flat-roofed room over, and an existing full-width single-storey flat-roofed rear extension plus a flat-roofed two-storey rear outrigger element on part of the plan. Neighbour no.117 (street-right / garden-left) is a white detached house whose boundary-side garage and white polycarbonate/conservatory-type structure sit close to the shared boundary; neighbour no.113 (street-left / garden-right) is the larger house whose rear wing/roof comes within a very narrow gap (the stated ~1.25m alleyway) of 115's two-storey rear projection, and it has an obscure-glazed first-floor window facing the gap. Boundary treatments are timber close-board fencing both sides at the rear and a low fence/wall to the front drive. Rear flat-roof height sits just below first-floor cill level (~2.9-3.1m estimated); main eaves ~5.2-5.5m, ridge ~7.5-8m (estimates from door height and brick coursing).

facts.detail: Detached. Clear fenced gap between 115's integral garage and no.117's garage on one side (photo 35); narrow ~1.25m gap to no.113's rear wing on the other side (photo 39). Not physically attached to either neighbour.
Two storeys plus roof void. Main hipped roof with no existing dormers visible to the rear; loft appears unconverted externally (only a satellite dish and chimneys on the rear slope).

Main roof is hipped on both sides to the rear (clay plain tiles, moss-stained). Front has a projecting mock-Tudor half-timbered gable over the two-storey bay (street-left). A brick chimney with red pot rises through the rear slope right-of-centre (garden view); a second stack sits at the 113-side flank. Rear hipped form limits easy loft conversion without hip-to-gable or large dormer.
facts.value: Hipped main roof, front feature gable

facts.detail: Integral garage at the front, on the RIGHT as viewed from the street, with dark (black) up-and-over style opening flush with the front elevation. Above it is a flat-roofed first-floor section with two windows — i.e. an existing two-storey front/side addition whose roof is lower than the main hipped roof.
facts.value: Integral front garage, street-right, room over with flat roof

facts.detail: Full-width single-storey rear extension, cream/white render, flat felt roof with black fascia. Rear elevation (garden view): small obscure window and half-glazed uPVC door on the LEFT, large fixed kitchen window centre-left, and a 4-panel uPVC French/patio door set on the RIGHT. Flat roof line runs continuously across the whole rear and wraps toward the 117 side. Render is stained/blowing in places with a vertical crack above the patio doors.

On part of the rear (toward the 113 side / garden-right area) there is an existing flat-roofed, parapet-edged TWO-storey rendered projection with a first-floor window (bottles visible on cill — likely bathroom) and a white flue/soil-vent pipe rising past the flat roof. Its flat roof sits below the main hipped ridge, roughly at main-eaves level. This is the element that comes closest to no.113's roof slope across the narrow gap.

facts.topic: Neighbour no.117 — side and rear form
facts.detail: No.117 is on the RIGHT viewed from the street, therefore on the LEFT viewed from the rear garden. White rendered detached house with two-storey bay, half-timbered gable and a green-doored garage/annex hard against the boundary with 115 under a small pitched red-tile canopy. Aerial view shows a long white ribbed (polycarbonate/conservatory-type) roof structure on 117's boundary side facing 115, plus a white flat-roofed rear addition — consistent with the described conservatory at 117. Rear photo 37 shows this white glazed structure at the far left edge behind tarpaulin-covered items.
facts.value: 117 = street-right / garden-left; conservatory + garage on boundary

facts.topic: Neighbour no.113 — side and rear form
facts.detail: No.113 is on the LEFT viewed from the street, therefore on the RIGHT viewed from the rear garden. Larger house with big hipped clay-tile roof and a substantial dark flat-roofed rear addition visible on the aerial. Its rear wing/roof slope comes within a very narrow gap of 115's two-storey rear projection (the ~1.25m alleyway); a small OBSCURE-GLAZED first-floor window in 113's flank faces this gap (photo 39) — a side-facing window relevant to 45-degree/outlook tests. A red-brick two-storey rear elevation of 113 with modern windows is visible beyond the fence at garden-right (photo 37/40).
facts.value: 113 = street-left / garden-right; own rear extension, obscure flank window

facts.detail: Front: fully block-paved (herringbone) drive across the frontage, low concrete-post/timber remnant wall to the footpath, close-board timber fence on the 117 boundary beside the garage, low brick pier/wall at 117's drive entrance. Rear: timber close-board/panel fencing on the 113 side (garden-right) and a woven/panel fence on the 117 side visible at the far corner; rear garden beyond 115's extension is mostly paved slabs then rough lawn with a small tree close to the rear elevation.

Using the rear door (~2.03m) and render band lines: single-storey rear extension flat roof/fascia approx 2.9-3.1m, sitting just below first-floor window cills. First-floor window heads ~4.8m; main eaves ~5.2-5.5m; hipped ridge estimated ~7.5-8.0m. The over-garage flat-roof section at the front is roughly at main-eaves height. The two-storey rear outrigger parapet is approximately at or just above main-eaves level.

Rear elevation carries: black rainwater downpipe at the garden-left end of the extension; brown/copper-coloured downpipe from the main roof discharging onto the extension flat roof; black soil pipe near the patio; large white flue/soil-vent pipe up the two-storey outrigger (113 side); satellite dish on rear roof slope (117 side) and another on the chimney near 113; two solar-powered security floodlights and vent grilles on the rear wall. All would need diverting/rebuilding within a 6m+ deep extension.

Rear first floor has: a small obscure-glazed window at the garden-left end (bathroom/WC), a clear casement window centre-left with net curtain, a top-hung open casement centre-right, and the outrigger window on the 113 side. These indicate at least one habitable room plus bathrooms at first-floor rear — relevant to how a 4m first-floor addition would re-plan the rear rooms.

White render with black detailing: two-storey canted/square bay under the half-timbered gable (street-left), arched brick door surround painted black/white with '115' on a white panelled door (centre), small landscape window to its left, garage to the right, two first-floor windows over the garage under a flat roof. TV aerial and small dish at the chimney. Street is a mature suburban avenue of large detached/semi inter-war houses with grass verges and trees.

Aerial screenshot 00000022 confirms plot layout: 115 between 113 (toward the road junction) and 117; 115 already shows a large dark flat-roofed rear addition. Second aerial (00000027) is centred on 8 Colmore Rd, the road backing/adjoining to the south — a large hipped-roof property with wide rear additions and outbuildings, evidently the 'precedent in area' the owner refers to. Long rear gardens (~30m+) mean rear-garden amenity space is not a limiting factor for a 6-6.7m extension.
No significant level change visible: rear patio slabs run level from the extension threshold to the lawn; front drive falls gently to the street. Thresholds appear near-flush at the rear doors.

From the STREET facing the front: garage and no.113 side on the RIGHT is INCORRECT — garage is street-RIGHT but that is the no.117 side; no.113 is street-LEFT (bay/gable side). From the REAR GARDEN facing the house this mirrors: no.117 (conservatory) is garden-LEFT, no.113 (1.25m gap, obscure flank window, own extension) is garden-RIGHT. The existing two-storey flat-roof rear outrigger of 115 is at the garden-right (113) side of the rear elevation.

open_questions: Confirm on the ground which flank the 2005 (~3.3m) permission related to and whether the existing full-width flat-roof extension exceeds it — the aerial suggests the built extension is deeper/wider than a 3.3m span.

Verify numbering direction on Vicarage Rd from a doorstep check or Street View: the left/right assignment of 113 vs 117 rests on the aerial label positions and one oblique street photo (photo 35's neighbour with the green garage door assumed to be 117).
Whether no.113's obscure-glazed flank window over the alleyway is a habitable-room or non-habitable window (affects impact assessment).
Exact depth of 115's existing rear extension and of 113's and 117's rear projections — needs measurement; photos alone cannot give reliable metre figures.
Whether the loft is already converted internally (no rear dormer/rooflights visible, but front/side rooflights were not photographed).
